about: Sound-alike substitutions for whole-word variants (Q4), substituted stems (Q5) and endings (Q6). One substitution at a time, then pairs, tier by tier, until the cap. Tier 1 = the strongest sound-alikes (the hinge consonant and QU); tier 2 = vowel and ending spellings; tier 3 = cosmetic.

rows.why: Z and S sound alike between vowels (EQUAZIA / EQUASIA); a search on one spelling misses the other.
A doubled consonant is pronounced the same; registrants double letters to stylise a mark.
X is a common stylised stand-in for the Z and S sounds in software marks.
QU is pronounced KW; phonetic respellings (EKWA-) are common and read as the same word.
Dropping the U after Q is a common stylisation (EQAZIA) with the same sound.
K is a hard-sound respelling of QU in coined marks.
CU is the Spanish and Italian spelling of the same sound (ECUA-).
IA and IYA are pronounced alike; an ending respelled with Y reads the same.
YA is a shortened spelling of the IA ending with the same sound.
EA and IA endings are confused in speech and in memory.
An added H changes the spelling, not the sound.
An initial E and AE are pronounced alike (AEQUA- / EQUA-).
An initial E is often heard, and spelled, as I.
A doubled consonant and a single one sound the same (EQUALL / EQUAL); each spelling is searched.
